profile.background: CS master; Python + TypeScript; several agent demos; no big-tech internship. Goal: create verifiable systems evidence rather than another generic chatbot.

trends.name: Agent Reliability / Eval
trends.note: Production agents create demand for eval, observability and reliability.

trends.name: Context Engineering
trends.note: Increasingly explicit role in agent performance and cost control.

trends.name: Generic RAG
trends.note: Easy to reproduce; weak differentiation unless domain/data moat exists.

wedge.name: Agent Reliability / Evaluation
wedge.thesis: Demand is moving from demo quality to production reliability. Talent supply is thinner than generic agent application roles, and proof is benchmarkable in days.
wedge.killCriteria: Target companies show no eval/reliability signal across a meaningful sample, or a 3-day prototype cannot produce a measurable result.
wedge.nextTest: Build a fixed-task harness benchmark and compare baseline vs retry + memory + context-policy variants.

claims.claim: Built an agent reliability benchmark across a fixed task set
claims.ownership: Benchmark design, retry policy, context strategy
claims.risk: Why these tasks? How was success scored?

claims.claim: Improved completion rate from baseline after harness changes
claims.risk: Control for model/version variance and benchmark bias

position.safe: AI / Agent Application Engineer with hands-on evaluation and reliability work.
position.stretch: Agent Systems Engineer focused on harness reliability and evaluation.
position.gaps: Production observability; external users; contribution to a real agent/eval codebase.

applications.next: Find engineering owner and map current reliability pain

interview.weakness: Need stronger explanation of task selection, repeated trials and model-version controls.
interview.drill: If retry, memory or context policy is removed one by one, which change matters most and why?
